name: spotpixels
tagline: A Million Dollar Homepage style grid where you buy a block of pixels once and it stays there with your image and link.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software here is a grid of tiles with images and links, plus a checkout. An agent can produce that before your coffee goes cold, and the result will look fine. What you cannot produce is the thing you were actually buying: other people looking at that specific grid, and other people having already paid for squares on it, which is the only reason a square on it is worth anything. A pixel grid with one advertiser is a personal homepage with extra steps. Build it if you want a fun artifact, not if you want the outcome.
coreLoopDIY: Renders a static pixel grid from a JSON manifest of tiles, each with an image, a link and coordinates, on your own domain.
requirements: Node 20 and a static host or any cheap VPS
Your own images, cropped to tile size
A domain, if you want anyone to ever see it
whatYouLose: Traffic, which was the entire product
Other advertisers on the same canvas, so no reason for anyone to visit
Payment handling, invoices and refunds for buyers
Link moderation, so nothing stops you shipping a dead or malicious URL
The implied promise that someone else keeps the page online for years
moatNotes: Two sided in the cheapest possible way: buyers pay for attention, visitors come for the spectacle of a filled grid, and neither shows up first.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the purchase is not a piece of software, it is a spot on a page that already exists and already gets looked at. The novelty of a permanent one time placement only works when the canvas is shared with strangers, and the price of a tile is really a bet on the operator keeping the domain renewed and the page indexed. Cloning the grid gives you the mechanic without the crowd, which is like printing your own billboard and hanging it in your garage.
notes: The grid is an afternoon; the audience is not. The moat is a filled canvas and the strangers who come to stare at it.
prompt:
Build a static pixel grid site, the Million Dollar Homepage mechanic, single owner edition. No accounts, no payments, no analytics, no telemetry.

Stack: Node 20, TypeScript, Vite with vanilla TS, no framework. Output a fully static build in dist/ that works on any static host.

Data model: content/tiles.json, an array of objects { id, x, y, w, h, image, href, title }. Coordinates and sizes are in grid cells, not pixels. Grid is 100 by 100 cells, each cell 10 by 10 CSS pixels, so the canvas is 1000 by 1000.

Build step:
1. Read content/tiles.json and validate it: integer coords, tiles fully inside the grid, no overlapping tiles. On any failure, print the offending tile ids and exit non zero.
2. Copy tile images from content/images/ into dist/images/, and resize each one with sharp to exactly its tile pixel dimensions.
3. Emit dist/index.html with the grid as absolutely positioned anchor tags inside a 1000 by 1000 container, plus a subtle CSS background grid for empty cells.

Frontend behaviour:
- Hovering a tile shows a tooltip with its title and destination host, no JS framework, one small script file.
- All outbound links get target="_blank" and rel="noopener nofollow".
- Responsive: scale the whole 1000 by 1000 canvas with CSS transform on narrow screens, never reflow tiles.
- A short header, a tile count, and total cells sold out of 10000.

Also ship:
- scripts/add-tile.ts, a CLI that takes id, x, y, w, h, image path, href, title, appends to tiles.json and reruns validation.
- content/tiles.json seeded with three example tiles and placeholder images generated at build time if the files are missing.
- README with how to add a tile and how to deploy dist/ anywhere.

Out of scope, do not build: Stripe or any checkout, a reservation flow, user accounts, an admin UI, a backend server, a database, link health checking.

No secrets are needed. If you later add anything requiring keys, read them from .env and commit .env.example only.
